questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How fast food spread around the world from 1950s America
Why fast food is bad for your health
How to open a restaurant in Iceland
The best burger recipes in the world
questions.why: They discuss the global spread of fast food from its beginnings in 1950s America.

questions.q: Is Beth a fan of fast food?
options: Yes, she eats it every week and loves burgers
Yes, but only burgers
No, she never eats it
Not really, although it can be convenient
questions.why: Beth says 'not really', though sometimes it can be convenient because it's quick.

questions.q: According to author Adam Chandler, what was special about many fast food company founders?
options: They came from rich families
They had all studied business at top universities before starting
They had few qualifications or money but could still succeed
They had worked as chefs in Europe
questions.why: He says many didn't have degrees or come from money, giving a sense that 'anyone can do this'.

questions.q: According to Beth, what did the rise of fast food reflect?
options: The rise of farming in America
The growth of America's economic power after the Second World War
The growing popularity of American films and music around the world
A fall in the price of meat
questions.why: She says it reflected the rise of American economic power after the Second World War.

questions.q: What did brands like KFC and McDonald's symbolise for many people?
options: Unhealthy modern lifestyles
The idea that anyone can succeed through hard work
The end of family meals
Cheap food that only poor families would choose to eat
questions.why: Beth says they symbolised the American dream – success through hard work and determination.

questions.q: Why does Phil mention visiting two McDonald's on opposite sides of the planet?
options: To say the food is better abroad
To complain about long queues
To show that the same meal is now available all over the world
To explain why the prices of meals are so different in each country
questions.why: He says you can eat 'exactly the same meal' there, showing success wasn't limited to America.

questions.q: According to editor Andie Sophia Fontaine, why did McDonald's struggle in Iceland?
options: Icelanders don't eat meat
The government banned it immediately after the first restaurant opened
It was too far from the capital
Iceland already had its own long burger tradition
questions.why: She says Iceland had 'a long-standing burger culture' with its own version, the shop burger.

questions.q: What finally caused McDonald's to fail in Iceland?
options: The global financial crisis of 2008–2009
A new tax on burgers
A shortage of cucumbers
Strong competition from KFC and other brands
questions.why: She says the final nail in the coffin was the global financial crisis in 2008/2009.
